text: My read: **Trellis (ADR-0075) is a reconciliation substrate for the reactive *read* side** — graph transactions, dependency identity, collection diffs, scoped teardown, output-frame lifecycle, deterministic replay — living *below typed read sessions*. The wallet operation journal is a different animal: a **durable write-side saga** (`Draft→MintPending→MintSettled→PublishPending→Settled/Unknown/Failed`) whose whole job is crash-recovery and reconciling against *external* authority (the mint) so no double-spend/double-pay survives process death. [...] - **Saga (1)** writes **pre-effect**: "about to consume proofs A,B for a mint spend." That pre-record *is* the at-most-once mechanism. Durable, money-critical. [...] - **Trail (3)** writes **post-observation**: "a deletion arrived / a probe found C spent / a nutzap redeemed." Diagnostic, bounded. [...] - **State (2)** is the fold over the post-observation facts. [...] The load-bearing correction: **you can't read 2/3 out of 1**, because the saga only knows *locally-initiated* operations — and most of what makes the wallet chaotic (inbound token arrivals, NIP-09 deletions from your *other* devices, incoming nutzaps) never touches the saga at all. So it's not a subset relationship. It's **producer/consumer**: the saga *emits facts into* the trail (`MintSettled`, `Unknown→reconciled`, `Failed`) so the trail can explain locally-caused shape changes too — but their schemas never merge (money-critical pre-effect records must not live in a diagnostic log with bounded eviction).
